notes: Case 003 and 005 show no visible landlord-approval event before provider assignment (003 ev002 provider assigned directly). Not treated as conflict because absence is not contradiction; see gaps. In 004 ev002 approval precedes the quote, so it is approval-in-principle of the job, not of the quote. [B2] Approval appears to be two-stage: job/provider-selection approval (system status), then quote approval. In 006/007/008 a provider was assigned to quote before the landlord saw the quote, so P-001 covers instructing works, not obtaining a quote. 007 ev002 shows approval with no landlord message visible. Cases 009 and 010 are tenant-only tasks with no landlord approval step (distinguishing condition, not used to resolve). [B3] 013: landlord was told, not asked, for an appliance repair (no quote step). 012: a note records a prior landlord agreement, so no new request was made. [B5] 022: provider assigned and sent to attend with no landlord contact anywhere in the case (a routine lock fault). Landlord approval was asked first in 021, 023, 024, 025. [B6] Tell-and-proceed (landlord informed or never contacted) now appears in 013, 022, 029, 030 against ask-first in 15+ cases. All four are routine, low-cost, no-quote-expected faults, but nothing states that as the rule. [B7] 034: approval logged with no landlord correspondence visible (offline or unlogged). [B8] 039: provider assigned about three days after the landlord hold with no landlord reply recorded (offline approval or tell-and-proceed). [B9] 043: provider assigned after about five days of landlord silence, before the landlord's later yes (a human acted).
decision: Default: ask the landlord and wait, unless the case already records their agreement. A defensible alternative for routine no-quote faults is to tell the landlord and proceed (013, 022, 029, 030), but we do not adopt it without evidence of a limit.

evidence.quote: unable to ascertain this was re the dishwasher

statement: Landlord invoices may be settled out of the rent; tell the landlord the amount.
trigger: Contractor invoice received on a rent-managed property.
action: Email landlord that the invoice will come from the rent.

evidence.quote: deduct it off the rental amount

notes: Only case. Not evidenced whether landlord consent is needed or any limit applies.

statement: When the landlord offers a self-help workaround for a minor fault, relay it to the tenant, tell the landlord the outcome, and close unless the tenant comes back.
trigger: Minor fault; landlord suggests trying a fix first and a contractor only if needed.
action: Do not instruct a contractor; relay workaround; close; reopen on recurrence.

evidence.quote: I will close this down unless she comes back to us
There is a switch to the righthand side of the hob
we will close this job down now
approves the tenant to fix the door

notes: [B4] 017: no landlord outcome message is logged before closing.
decision: Follow the landlord's lead on minor faults, but if the fault affects door/window/lock security, flag to a human instead of closing (see P-049).

statement: Close a task with no cost incurred as 'completed without payment'.
trigger: Case closed with no contractor work or no payment due.
action: Complete with the without-payment status.

evidence.quote: Task has been completed without payment

notes: [B5] 024 used the same label although an invoice was received, so the label does not prove nothing was spent; 025 was a free warranty repair.

statement: If the landlord names a specific contractor, instruct that contractor and notify the tenant and contractor.
trigger: Landlord's reply names who should attend.
action: Assign that provider, email the tenant and the contractor.

evidence.quote: Please get Imogen to have a look at it

statement: After a repair, tell the landlord about any recurrence risk or recommended replacement; do not order a replacement without their decision.
trigger: Contractor reports an underlying condition.
action: Email the landlord the finding.

statement: For faults that may affect home security (door will not latch, lock, glass), keep the tenant informed and ask them to report any security concern; treat as routine unless evidence says otherwise.
trigger: Door/lock/window fault.
action: Interim email to tenant while waiting on the landlord; do not close with the fault unresolved.
notes: 014: tenant relayed a warning that the door could shatter glass; the agency still applied the landlord's workaround and closed. 015: handled as routine. [B5] 021, 022, 023: stiff or broken door locks and a snapped key were all handled as routine with no urgency or security advice. Our escalate-same-day default for unsecurable doors still stands. [B8] 037: a leaking shower hose was handled as routine with no interim advice.
decision: No emergency handling is evidenced. Escalate to a human the same day if a door/window/lock cannot be secured, glass is cracked, or the tenant reports a security risk; do not wait for landlord approval in that case.

statement: If a contractor's reply is empty or unreadable, a human takes over; the agent must not invent its content, dates or amounts.
trigger: Inbound contractor email has no usable text.
action: Flag for manual handling.
notes: Same empty-email pattern in 013 ev011/017. [B7] The real content arrived in the next event; do not act on the unreadable one.

statement: If the landlord has not replied by the 3-day flag, re-send the request, hold, and keep chasing by phone and email; never proceed without approval.
trigger: Landlord silent after the first request.
action: Re-email (trim to the fault), call, remind; hold Waiting for Landlord.

evidence.quote: Please advise if you would like us to send one of our contractors

notes: No chaser count or spacing is evidenced.
decision: After repeated unanswered chasers, escalate to a human with a case summary; never decide spend or scope for the landlord (case 019 chased for about two months).

statement: If a quote rises after the landlord approved it, get approval again for the new amount; an old approval does not cover a higher price.
trigger: Revised quote above the approved figure.
action: Explain the reason and new figure to the landlord; hold until a fresh reply.

evidence.quote: the quote is going to be around

notes: Case 019: approval at the first figure, then a revised quote was sent for approval again. The figures are examples, not thresholds.

statement: If the contractor finds nothing to fix and no invoice is due, tell the landlord the outcome and close without payment.
trigger: Contractor reports no work needed.
action: Thank contractor, email landlord, close as completed without payment.

statement: A newly used provider with no portal access invoices by email; record the invoice and assigned provider manually.
trigger: Provider not set up on the portal.
action: Note it, set provider via manual mode change, forward invoice.

statement: For routine inspections, notify the tenant by SMS and email with the visit window and management-key access; reschedule on request by phone, rebook and cancel the old slot.
trigger: Routine inspection due or tenant asks to move it.
action: Send notice; on tenant request call, agree new date, cancel old booking, confirm by email/SMS.

evidence.quote: we will access using our management key

statement: After an inspection, email the landlord a summary with the full report and record whether issues were found; minor tenant-caused marks are left to the tenant to make good.
trigger: Inspection results added.
action: Email landlord, upload the report, mark Inspection issues YES/NO.

evidence.quote: Download the full inspection report here

notes: 020: the email said no issues were identified while the report itself listed a tenant-fitted item and a defect. Do not copy the summary line blindly.

statement: If a landlord's reply to an inspection raises permission (e.g. an unapproved fixture) or key custody, hand it to a human; do not grant permission or invent where keys are.
trigger: Landlord email after inspection raises a tenancy or key question.
action: Flag for a human with the case context.

evidence.quote: dog flap installation that was not approved

decision: Escalate. No policy on permissions or key custody is evidenced.

statement: Dispatch a contractor to attend and quote only 'if the job requires quotation'; a minor fix done on site needs no quote.
trigger: Routine repair (lock, key, small fault) where the landlord has agreed to a contractor attending.
action: Tell the contractor to quote and wait only if a quote is needed; skip the quote step when the fix is made on site.

evidence.quote: No quote required, repaired on site

notes: Cost of such on-site fixes was never discussed in 021-024.
decision: Landlord's go-ahead to attend covers a minor on-site fix; anything needing a quote or extra cost goes back to the landlord first.

statement: If the landlord names a prior installer or warranty route, contact that party first; do not accept 'out of warranty' as final or authorise paid work until the position is verified.
trigger: Landlord points to a previous fitter or the appliance may be under warranty.
action: Phone the installer, send the job, chase, relay only the verified warranty position to the landlord.
notes: 025: the first 'out of warranty' answer was later contradicted; the tenant went about a month without an oven. Correct the landlord if an earlier update proves wrong. [B8] 036: the landlord said the taps were under guarantee; the same contractor then replaced the faulty tap at no charge. Nothing contradicts the rule. [B9] 041: the landlord went to the original installer himself.

statement: Before closing, tell the landlord the outcome (fixed, no work needed, recurrence risk, cost route).
trigger: Work finished or no work needed.
action: Short email to the landlord, then close.

evidence.quote: I just wanted to let you know
Your landlord said it's fine to replace it with your own
the window issue was now resolved
the window repair is now complete

notes: [B6] Most cases (021-030) close with no landlord outcome message, including 026-030. Flagged as a conflict between our decision and the common practice. [B7] 034 is a clean example: outcome plus invoice emailed to the landlord before closing. [B8] 040 is the clearest failure: the landlord agreed to a check, was never answered, closed with 'no further action', and chased afterwards. [B9] 042 and 043 told the landlord the fix and the cost before closing. [B10] 047, 048: closed with no outcome message to the landlord logged.
decision: Always send the landlord a short outcome message before closing. Cases 021-025 closed without one and we treat that as a gap, not a pattern to copy.

statement: Unrelated issues raised on an open request (e.g. a fence, a roof leak) must not be answered or claimed fixed in it; open a separate request.
trigger: Tenant raises another problem on an open or closed case.
action: Log it as its own request; closing message covers only what this request fixed.

evidence.quote: have both been fixed and everything
contacted block management on your behalf

notes: 024: the closing email claimed the fence was fixed with nothing in the case supporting it; a later leak report after closing got no reply. [B6] 027: a new parking query on a closed task was answered in the same record.
decision: Answer the tenant's new point, but log it as its own request; never claim it fixed under the old one.

statement: A minor tenant-responsibility fault (e.g. a blocked internal drain) gets a tenant-responsibility notice with self-help steps and a warning that call-out and repair are billed to the tenant; no landlord or contractor is involved.
trigger: Tenant reports a blockage or similar fault that is theirs to clear.
action: Email self-help steps and the cost warning; chase once; close when the tenant confirms it is fixed.

evidence.quote: the full cost of the call-out and repair will be billed

notes: The tenancy clause is asserted by the agency only; no tenancy terms are visible. Cause was assumed before any inspection.
decision: Use only for clearly tenant-side minor blockages. If the cause is unclear, or there is a flood or leak risk, ask for details and involve the landlord or escalate.

statement: If a tenant does not respond to a self-help request, send one chase with a stated close-down deadline plus an SMS, then close if still silent.
trigger: Self-help request unanswered.
action: Chase email and SMS naming the deadline, hold, close if no reply.

evidence.quote: Should we not hear back from you within the next 24hrs

notes: The 24-hour figure is an example, not a policy.

statement: If the tenant disputes the visit date, do not adjudicate; the date confirmed with the contractor stands.
trigger: Tenant's date differs from the booked visit.
action: Tell the tenant to go by the contractor-confirmed date and hold waiting for the provider.

evidence.quote: if Keystone Compliance have confirmed a date with you

statement: After a repair, phone the tenant to confirm the fix works before closing.
trigger: Work reported complete.
action: Call the tenant; close on their confirmation.

evidence.quote: working properly after the recent repair

notes: [B7] Absent in 031, 032, 034, 035 (no tenant fix-confirmation before close).

statement: If the tenant says damage pre-dated their tenancy, record it and continue the repair; do not assign blame.
trigger: Cause of damage asked and tenant denies it.
action: Log the reply, proceed.

evidence.quote: at the time I was mooving in

decision: Do not decide liability. Flag any deposit or liability question to a human.

statement: If the tenant offers to replace a landlord-supplied appliance with their own, get the landlord's consent first; the replacement is the tenant's property and liability, and no contractor is sent.
trigger: Tenant proposes their own replacement instead of a repair.
action: Ask the landlord (and whether they will cover removal of the old unit); relay the answer; note ownership and liability.

evidence.quote: willing to replaced the machine with her own
see what they would like to do

notes: 038: removal cost cover was offered to the tenant by the agency on the landlord's brief 'Yes this is fine'; the landlord never confirmed the cost cover explicitly.
decision: Get the landlord's explicit yes on both the swap and any removal-cost cover before telling the tenant.

statement: Do not close a request while a commitment to the landlord or tenant is still open (e.g. a promised check); record it as a follow-up or hold, and answer the landlord.
trigger: Landlord has agreed to an action or asked for an update and the agency has promised something later.
action: Keep the case open on hold, or create the follow-up, and reply to the landlord.

evidence.quote: seeking an update on the washing machine repair request

notes: Single case; counted as a failure example, not an agency rule.
decision: Our rule. In 040 the agency promised a later check, closed with 'no further action', and the landlord had to chase.

statement: If the contractor's earlier work was faulty and they replace it, no charge applies; record the reason and close without payment.
trigger: Repeat visit for a defect in the contractor's own earlier work or an item under guarantee.
action: Chase for photos and confirmation; close as completed without payment once the contractor confirms.
notes: 036: about six weeks of chasing; the landlord complained of delay and missing photos; the agency kept holding and never reassigned the job.

statement: A landlord's go-ahead may cover only a simple fix; if parts or complexity arise, the contractor must quote and wait for further approval.
trigger: Landlord approves attendance without a price.
action: Pass the conditional scope to the contractor; any quote goes back to the landlord.

evidence.quote: needs part or is more complex, please quote it

notes: Supports P-002/P-058; no spend limit is stated.

statement: Before giving a tenant's contact details to a landlord's own contractor, get the tenant's consent.
trigger: Landlord's contractor asks for the tenant's contact details.
action: Phone the tenant, get authorisation, then pass them on.

evidence.quote: gave authorisation to pass on her details

notes: [B10] 046: tenant's number was emailed to the contractor with no consent step logged; 050 ev24 also sent tenant details (a different name) to the contractor. Consent is our safer default.
decision: Our decision: get tenant consent (or confirm on the thread that the tenant agreed) before passing a number to a contractor; never send another person's details.

statement: If the request is unclear, ask the tenant first (which item, was it landlord-requested) before approaching the landlord.
trigger: Tenant report lacks the detail needed to brief the landlord.
action: Email the tenant, hold Waiting for Tenant, then write to the landlord with the detail.

evidence.quote: Was this requested by your landlord?

statement: If the landlord restricts scope for budget reasons, do not pursue the deferred items.
trigger: Landlord approves part of the work only.
action: Instruct or track only the approved part; note the deferred item.

evidence.quote: budget for the windows for now

statement: When the landlord's reply or the contractor's findings give alternatives (e.g. handle or lock), relay the priced options with VAT to the landlord rather than choosing; a blanket 'proceed with whatever is needed' then covers either.
trigger: Contractor reply is ambiguous on the fault or offers options.
action: Send options and prices to the landlord, then tell the contractor to proceed as approved; do not trust an unreadable summary as the quote.

evidence.quote: Please go ahead with whatever needed

notes: Closing note records a quote given (49.40 incl VAT) that matches neither option; figures are examples.

statement: Ask the contractor to send the invoice as a PDF.
trigger: Visit date has passed and the invoice is outstanding.
action: Ask whether the job was done and request a PDF invoice.

statement: If a tenant withdraws part of a multi-issue request, tell the landlord and tenant and continue only with what remains.
trigger: Tenant says one of several faults is fixed.
action: Email landlord the narrowed scope, confirm to tenant, hold. If the landlord replies about a different scope or address, restate what remains.

evidence.quote: My mother managed to fix the toilet.
It is just the window issue that needs to be assessed now.

statement: For a minor fault the tenant offers to fix, ask the landlord whether the tenant may self-fix or a contractor is wanted; relay it, chase once for confirmation, and close without payment if fixed or no reply.
trigger: Tenant reports a minor fault and is willing to fix it.
action: No contractor until the tenant says they cannot; one chase stating the job will close without a reply.

Please let me know if not and I will then get a contractor
if no reply will close off the job
